top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a mature, experimentally verified achievement with a clean two-person allocation: Katori's founding idea of magic-wavelength trapping, which cancels the lattice light shift so many atoms can be interrogated at once, and Ye's realization at the 1e-18 level. It has been reproduced independently in Sr and Yb at several laboratories, and it delivers results about nature (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, constraints on varying constants and dark-matter couplings) as well as a better instrument. The citation scope in P001 is bounded to the invention and realization of the clock. I am the member least at home in metrology and would defer to the specialists on fine points, but I see no reason to prefer no award to a prize that meets the discovery-first test.
